Dear Customer,

Thank you for contacting TOPENS. This is Joyce from TOPENS Customer Service Team. It will be a pleasure to assist you today.

I apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused, but do not worry, we will do our best to help you. All TOPENS products are backed by a 12-month warranty.

Checked with our engineer, please help us do some tests to find out the problem, so that we can provide corresponding help.

1. Please measure the voltage of the +BAT- terminals (11# and 12#) on the control board to see whether it is above 22VDC. If the voltage is below 22VDC and you are using a battery, please disconnect the solar panels from the TCS3 solar charge controller, disconnect the TCS3 controller from the control board, and test the output voltage of the batteries. If the battery voltage is below 22VDC, please charge the batteries fully with an additional charger and connect the batteries to the +BAT- terminals (11# and 12#) on the control board, then press the remote to see whether it can work. If it can work in this case, please reconnect the TCS3 back to see whether it can still work. If not, the TCS3 is defective. If you are using an AC adapter, please check whether the output voltage of the adapter is 36VDC, then disconnect the batteries and measure whether the battery output voltage is above 22VDC. Also, please check the POWER LED on the control board. If the POWER LED is off, please replace the fuse from the manual pack.

2. Disconnect all accessories from the control board first (just leave the power source and the arm). And disable the photocell function by turning the DIP switch #3 off. Then erase all remote codes from the control board and reprogram them to have a try. If it fails, please instantaneously short (plug the wire in, then pull it out immediately) the push button terminals (4# and 5#) to check whether the opener can work. Here is a video reference for how to instantaneously short the terminals: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VdDhyHZxmpQE5pG7BYHOJi5GYb7iZHFS/view?usp=sharing

3. Please check the motor. Connect the red & black wires of the arm to a DC 24V power source directly, the motor should run, and then exchange the polarity of the wires, the motor should run in the opposite direction. If the motor runs in both directions, the motor itself is good. If the motor does not run, it may be defective.

4. Disconnect the BLUE, GREEN & YELLOW wires of the faulty arm from the control board, use two jumper wires to short the ULT, COM & DLT terminals to which the wires were connected, and then press the remote to test whether the opener can work in both directions.

Please let me know the result one by one.

Videos showing the problem and pictures of the whole control board are much appreciated for further judgement. You can directly send the video to my E-mail via the attachment. If the sending is not successful, please share the photo or video link through dropbox, icloud or google drive. Thanks for your understanding and cooperation.

And also please reply your specific SHIPPING ADDRESS with zip code and confirm PHONE # available for further assistance.

Thank you again for being a valued customer! Your complete satisfaction is what we strive for. We at TOPENS are always standing by and ready to help.

Best regards,
Joyce
TOPENS Customer Service Team

results.generated_reply_en:
Dear Customer,

Thank you for contacting TOPENS. This is Joyce from TOPENS Customer Service Team. It will be a pleasure to assist you today.

I understand you'd like to know the differences between the A8132, PW802, AD8, and AT1202 gate openers. I'm happy to clarify.

All four models use an 80W motor, but they differ in arm design, control board, and power supply method:

1. The A8132, PW802, and AD8 share the same A8 arm and an energy-saving control board. The AT1202 uses the AT12 arm and a standard control board with a digital display.

2. The A8132 includes the UPS01 power supply, which supports AC power, battery backup, and a 20W solar panel.

3. The AD8 is designed for battery-powered operation as its main power source. To connect AC power, you would need to add either the DPS180-U or the UPS01 unit separately.

4. The PW802 connects directly to AC power using the DPS180-U adapter, without battery or solar capability on that adapter.

5. The AT1202 has a built-in transformer for direct AC power and supports battery backup only.

Here are the purchasing links for these models and some compatible accessories, if you are in the US:
